title: Introduction to the Ultrasound Targeted Microbubble Destruction Technique
protocol: Mix 200 mg of 1,2-dipalmitoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphatidylcholine with 50 mg of 1,2-dipalmitoyl-sn-glycero-3-phosphatidylethanolamine and 1 g of glucose in 10 ml of PBS.
Heat the mixture in a boiling water bath for 20 to 30 minutes, pipetting every 5 minutes.
Store the solution at 4°C for up to 6 months.
Take 250 μl of the prepared microbubble stock and incubate at 40°C for 15 minutes.
Transfer the pre-warmed microbubble solution to a 1.5 mL microtube containing 50 μl of glycerol.
Add 1-2 mg of purified plasmid DNA encoding an expression construct for the gene of interest, with an optimal concentration of 4 mg/ml.
Add phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) to reach a final volume of 500 μl.
Replace the air in the microtube with Octafluoropropane gas.
Shake the mixture vigorously in a dental amalgamator for 20 seconds.
Remove the subnatant containing residual DNA and buffer carefully.
Wash the microbubble layer three times with sterile PBS to remove unattached DNA, placing on ice between each wash cycle.
Place plasmid DNA-bound microbubbles on ice for up to two hours until use.
Remove the subnatant from the microtube after mixing and PBS washes.
Measure the optical density of the removed solution at a wavelength of 260nm using a spectrophotometer.
Calibrate a 1 MHz cavitation transducer before first use to ensure proper mechanical index and pulse repetition.
Connect a 1 MHz, 13mm, unfocused submergible transducer to a 20 MHz Function/Arbitrary Waveform Generator through a power amplifier.
Place the transducer in a plastic container filled with water, aimed directly at a hydrophone connected to a 500 MHz oscilloscope via a charge amplifier.
Modify waveform, frequency, amplitude, burst cycle, and power amplification to obtain proper duty cycle and mechanical index optimal for cavitation of microbubbles.
Calibrate the system to a mechanical index equivalent to ~1.3 at 1 MHz.
Anesthetize C57BL/6 mice with 100mg/kg ketamine and 5mg/kg xylazine through IP injection prior to microbubble delivery and UTMD.
Administer microbubble delivery intravenously through direct injection into the left ventricle of the heart or through tail vein catheterization.

Inject up to 100 μl of plasmid DNA-loaded microbubble solution directly into the left ventricle of the heart using a 30 gauge needle inserted at the anterior 4th intercostal space under ultrasonic visualization.
Add NaOH to achieve a stock concentration of 1.25 mg/ml for leptin.
Prepare fresh working solutions for injection 30 minutes before each time point.
Visualize microbubble injection using a Visual Sonics’ 38 MHz high frequency ultrasound transducer in long-axis view.
Place the ultrasound transducer on the thorax of the mouse in a stationary position.
Destroy microbubbles with a second, smaller sized low frequency 1.0 MHz transducer over the desired organ.
Administer ultrasound to the liver at a pulse repetition frequency of 1.0 MHz and mechanical index of 1.3-1.5.
Use a pulse repetition period of 100 ms for every 20 cycles for microbubble destruction.
Anesthetize the mouse appropriately for tail vein injection.
Insert a 27 gauge needle/tail vein catheter into the distal third of either the right or left lateral veins along the tail of the mouse.
Connect a syringe containing plasmid DNA-bound microbubbles to the needle/catheter.
Place the syringe in an infusion pump and set it to administer a uniform volume (200-300 μl) over 1 hour at a rate of 3 ml/hour.
Inject mice intraperitoneally with the luciferase reporter probe D-luciferin.
Anesthetize mice approximately 3 minutes after injection of D-luciferin.
Allow biodistribution of D-luciferin to proceed for ~10 minutes.
Place anesthetized mouse in the IVIS imaging chamber.
Take a full body image scan using the Xenogen In Vivo Imaging System (IVIS).
Measure photons emitted from the firefly luciferase/D-luciferin photochemical reaction during acquisition.
